newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares fall 2.6pct on foreign selling-broker.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares fall 2.6pct on foreign selling-broker.

text.p: Greek shares continued to falter on Monday on what floor traders described as foreign selling pressure. The benchmark index had lost more than 33 points hitting an intraday low of 1,450 points before cutting losses.

"There is large selling pressure on blue-chip banks and industrial stocks which are core holdings in foreign portfolios," said a floor trader. "Sell orders are placed by brokerages which typically execute on behalf of foreign institutional clients."
"It concerns me that there is no reaction from the buy side as we move to lower price levels, unlike what happened in recent months," the floor trader added.
Trading in OTE telecom was very active, with 1.3 million shares having changed hands by 1225 local (0925 GMT). The stock was holding at 6,600 drachmas.
Decliners led advancers 172 to 30 with 18 shares unchanged on a total of 220 traded.
Turnover amounted to 17.4 billion drachmas, with OTE contributing 8.5 billion. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
